ETCS-i Control
Through centralized control by the engine control computer, engine output relative to the accelerator opening is optimally controlled, achieving good accelerator controllability and vehicle stability over the entire driving range.
The functions of normal throttle opening control (non-linear control), idle speed control (ISC) and cruise control (models with cruise control system only) have been integrated into the 1-valve type electronically controlled throttle body.
Through integrated control with the powertrain system, excellent handling stability is ensured and comfort is improved.
To allow driving in the unlikely event of a malfunction, the system has a 2-system redundant configuration to ensure reliability.
ETCS-i Control List
Maximum Speed Control When the vehicle speed reaches 180km/h, the throttle valve is closed to restrict any increase in vehicle speed.
Idle Speed Control Controls the fast idle speed according to the engine coolant temperature and the idle speed after engine warm-up. In addition, the idle speed is controlled through the fuel injection volume and throttle opening.
Engine Control Block Diagram
Function List
Name Function
Air Flow Meter Detects the intake air temperature and intake air volume.
1-valve Electronically Controlled Throttle Body Throttle Position Sensor Detects the throttle valve opening angle.
Electronic Throttle Motor Controls the throttle valve opening angle according to driving conditions.
Accelerator Position Sensor Detects the accelerator opening.
Camshaft Position Sensor Detects the actual camshaft angle.
Crankshaft Position Sensor Detects the crank angle (engine speed).
Water Temperature Sensor Detects the engine coolant temperature.
Starter Relay Sends the starter voltage during engine starting as the starter signal.
Neutral Start Switch Detects the CVT P, N and D positions.
Combination Meter Receives the vehicle speed signal (SP1) and sends the vehicle speed signal (SPD).
